issuer: Florida Department of Revenue, Office of Technical Assistance
title: Florida DOR Technical Assistance Advisement 91B4-006: Condominium Association
subject: Condominium Association
text:
May 30, 1991
Re: Technical Assistance Advisement No. 91(B)4-006
Documentary Stamp Tax; Transfer of Recreational Properties
to a Condominium Association
XXX (hereinafter Associations)
XXX (hereinafter Maintenance Contractor)
XXX (hereinafter Fee Owner)
Dear
This is in response to your request for a Technical
Assistance Advisement concerning the tax as authorized by s.
201.02(1), F.S., as it applies to substantially the following
question:
Is the tax due where Fee owner deeds unencumbered
recreational properties to Associations for no
consideration other than Fee Owner's affiliate, Maintenance
Contractor, paying Associations money to settle contract
disputes, and in addition, cancelling all fixed fee
recreational maintenance contracts?
BACKGROUND
Associations are condominium owners' associations that
signed fixed fee maintenance agreements with Maintenance
Contractor with various expiration dates out to 1996.
Maintenance Contractor claimed to be losing money because yearly
increases in maintenance fees could not exceed the lesser of 6%
or the increase in the Consumer Price Index, and maintenance
Contractor, therefore, wished to cancel those contracts.
Maintenance fees paid by association members included $10 per
month per unit for use of the recreation facility, which
consists of a 6,500 sq. ft. building on approximately 2.2. acres
of land. Maintenance Contractor leased the facility from Fee
Owner, an affiliated company which is located outside Florida.
Since Fee owner wished to get rid of all its holdings in
Florida, it offered to give the facility to Associations for no

consideration other than the cancellation of the aforementioned
fixed fee contracts.
Maintenance Contractor expressed particular concern over a
provision in the contracts stating that Maintenance Contractor
was responsible for the "maintenance and servicing of the sewer
and water lines". Maintenance Contractor claimed that fixing
frequent breaks in those lines, especially breaks under paved
areas, was costly and a major contributor to the operating
losses of Maintenance Contractor. Therefore, in addition to
cancelling the fixed fee contract, maintenance Contractor paid
$160,000 to Associations to settle these disputes under the
maintenance contracts.
Fee owner will, without further consideration, execute and
deliver deeds to the recreational properties to each of the
Associations, one a 173/193 interest and the other a 20/193
interest.
Discussion and Law
Section 201.02(1), F.S., authorizes a tax upon instruments
which grant, transfer or otherwise convey an interest in land to
a "purchaser" for a "consideration". Consequently, to have a
taxable conveyance pursuant to s.201.02(1), F.S., it is
necessary that there be both a "purchaser" as well as
"consideration" for the transfer.
Section 201.02(1), F.S., obviously connotes the utilization
of the common meaning of "purchaser" as to one who obtains title
to real estate in consideration of the payment of money or its
equivalent. s. 201.02(1), F.S.; Fla. Admin. Code Rule 12B-
4.012(2)(a)(b); Culbreath v. Reid, 65 So.2d 556 (Fla. 1953).
Also, see Arias v. Springer, 42 N.M. 350, 78 P. 2d 153, 159
(N.M. 1938).
"Consideration" is an act or forbearance, or the promise
thereof, which is offered by one party to an agreement, and
accepted by the other as an inducement to that other's act or
promise." Black's Law Dictionary, 4th Ed. In order to be
taxable under Florida Statute 201.02, the document must be given

for a consideration that has monetary value which is reasonably
determinable. DeVore v Gay, 39 So.2d 796 (Fla. 1949): Culbreath
v. Reid, 65 So.2d 556 (Fla. 1953); Fla. Admin. Code Rules 12B-
4.012(2)(a)(b).
Florida Statute 201.02(1), as amended by s.7, 90-132, Laws
of Florida, now provides a definition of "consideration" which
includes the presumption that the fair market value of the real
property or interest therein is the basis for tax, but only in
that circumstance where the "consideration" paid or given in
exchange for the real property or interest therein includes
"property other than money". Florida Administrative Code Rule
12B-4.012(2)(b) gives a definition of "property other than
money".
Thus, it appears the legislative intent was not to change
the quid pro quo criterion for determining "consideration" under
s.201.02(1), but rather to change the basis for computing the
tax where something other than money is given as consideration
for the property.
DEPARTMENT'S POSITION
Fee owner deeded the property for no consideration other
than for it and its affiliate to back away from apparently a bad
business deal which has only continued over the years to grow
more costly to both.
We find no statutory or legal support to tax Fee Owner's
deeds transferring interest in the recreational properties to
Associations. Neither of the grantees paid "consideration" in
the form of money or its equivalent to be "purchasers" as
contemplated by s.201.02(1), F.S. Therefore, each deed would be
subject to no more than the minimal 55 cents tax. Fla. Admin.
Code Rules 12B-4.006(5), and 12B-4.012(6).
This response constitutes a Technical Assistance Advisement
under s. 213.22, F.S., which is binding on the Department only
under the facts and circumstances described in the request for
this advice as specified in s. 213.22, F.S. Our response is
predicated on those facts and the specific situation summarized

above. You are advised that subsequent statutory or
administrative rule changes or judicial interpretations of the
statutes or rules upon which this advice is based may subject
similar future transactions to a different treatment than
expressed in this response.
You are further advised that this response and your request
are public records under Chapter 119, F.S., which are subject to
disclosure to the public under the conditions of s. 213.22, F.S.
Your name, address, and any other details which might lead to
identification of the taxpayer must be deleted by the Department
before disclosure. In an effort to protect confidential
information, we request you notify the undersigned in writing
within 15 days of any deletions you wish made to the request or
this response.
Sincerely,
W.E. Webb
Technical Assistant
